 Emlyn Begley
 Most recent Most popular 'Everton will get chances' published at 19:13 GMT 19:13 GMT 
 Newcastle v Everton (20:00 GMT) 
 Everton's age-old problem is how Thierno Barry is going to perform because they rely so heavily on how well he is playing up front.
 To be fair to David Moyes's side, they carried more of a threat than I expected in their defeat by Arsenal and I can see them getting chances here, because Newcastle are so open.
 The Magpies will absolutely go for it again here and I have a sneaky feeling they will leave the door ajar for Everton to pinch the points.
 Sutton's prediction: 1-2

 get involved Get Involved published at 19:10 GMT 19:10 GMT

 I’m concerned for us and the management of game tactics. Matthias Jaissle is enthusiastic but I’m not getting the feeling of a team buy in like Eddie Howe created. Nor am I excited to watch the team, sadly. I fear things are going to get bad before they get better…
 Matt, Peterborough 
 21 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Grealish dropped because of fitness, not suspension published at 19:07 GMT 19:07 GMT 
 Newcastle v Everton (20:00 GMT) 
 Phil Munns 
BBC Radio Merseyside presenter 
 On Jack Grealish's absence... 
 We’re told that tonight, it is not a suspension from the club again like it was on Thursday. 
 This time, apparently it’s down to his fitness. We’re told he’s just not fit to play tonight or be involved at all.
 It is really worrying because one game, a suspension, it's done, then you think OK, you move past it, you put him back on the bench for tonight for example, but the fact that it’s two games suggests that there might be something a bit more serious at play here.
 33 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'No time to feel sorry for ourselves' published at 19:04 GMT 19:04 GMT 
 Newcastle v Everton (20:00 GMT) 
 Neil Johnston 
BBC Sport football reporter at St James' Park 
 Newcastle took 8,000 with them to Everton for last Thursday's Carabao Cup tie. Many were making their way home before the final whistle such was their team's poor showing on Merseyside.
 "There is no time to feel sorry for ourselves and make excuses - we have to learn quickly, understand what went wrong and where we need to be better," writes Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle in the match programme.
 "And then make sure we put it into action with a response on the pitch tonight. I have said many times we are going through a period of transition and we fully expect to experience ups and downs this season.
 "What's vital after nights like Thursday is that we all stick together, in the same way that we all celebrate together and enjoy the moment after wins like Crystal Palace."
 23 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:00 GMT 19:00 GMT 
 You can listen to the Monday Night Club at the top of this page or on BBC Radio 5 Live.
 Mark Chapman is joined by Chris Sutton, Shay Given and Rory Smith to discuss Arsenal's long awaited win at Anfield, Aston Villa taking issue with Jamie Carragher, and a good dose of Serie A on terrestrial TV nostalgia with James Richardson.
 14 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Steur hard done by not to start tonight published at 18:56 GMT 18:56 GMT 
 Newcastle v Everton (20:00 GMT) 
 John Anderson 
Former Newcastle defender on BBC Radio Newcastle 
 I feel for young Steur. I think he deserves his opportunity. 
 I thought when he came on last week the game was over but he wants to get on the ball, he wants to get on, try and make things happen but yet again he has to wait his turn. 
 I have to say I’m surprised. I thought there would have been one or two other changes there but that’s the way it is. 
 52 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Fancy seeing you again! published at 18:53 GMT 18:53 GMT 
 Newcastle v Everton (20:00 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Just four days ago, Everton hosted Newcastle in the Carabao Cup and beat them 3-1 to set up a quarter-final against League Two Fleetwood Town.
 Now attention turns to a Premier League game between the same opponents at St James' Park.
 Newcastle will be looking to make it back-to-back league wins after they beat Crystal Palace last weekend while Everton have lost their last two league games against Arsenal and Chelsea.
 28 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team news: Elanga starts for Newcastle; no Grealish again for Everton published at 18:50 GMT 18:50 GMT 
 Newcastle v Everton (20:00 GMT) 
 Neil Johnston 
BBC Sport football reporter at St James' Park 
 Anthony Elanga returns to the Newcastle United starting XI - one of two changes from the side that started the 3-1 Carabao Cup defeat at Everton last week.
 Joelinton is also back in the XI while Jacob Ramsey and Jacob Murphy drop to the bench.
 Newcastle starting XI: Hornicek, Dedic, Schar, Burn, Hall, Gonzalez,
Joelinton, Elanga, Willock, Barnes, Osula. 
 Subs: Pope, Botman,
Bamba, Wissa, Thiaw, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Ramsey.
 Once again Jack Grealish is not involved at all for Everton after a breach of club discipline.
 There is good news for the Toffees in the shape of Jarrad Branthwaite who is back in the starting XI after missing two games due to concussion protocols.
 Harrison Armstrong is also back from the start.
 Everton starting XI: Pickford, O'Brien, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko,
Armstrong, Garner, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry. 
 Subs:
 Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Johnson, Norgaard,
Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham.
 42 15 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 18:48 GMT 18:48 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' on this page to have your say 
 This will be a very tough game tonight. Newcastle will come flying out of the traps. Everton need to hold their nerve and avoid conceding on the first 15-20 mins. I see David Moyes reverting back to Harrison Armstrong in central midfield but hopefully plays Tyler Dibling ahead of the ineffective Brennan Johnson on the right wing.
 Mike, Liverpool
